entries.text: The MedICS window Everything happens in one window. Your tools open as tabs in the middle, and the panels around them give you the File Explorer, your workspace variables, the log, a terminal and the Python console. Extensions add their own tabs and menus. The MedICS main window. Tools open as tabs, with the File Explorer, workspace variables and the bottom panel (Logging · Terminal · Jupyter · Results) around them. Interface & components →

Features Area What you get Image I/O DICOM, TIFF stacks, HDF5 / .med , MATLAB .mat , PNG/JPEG, and other scientific formats Preview Double-click files in Explorer to inspect text, markdown, tables, 2-D images, and volumes (slice, window/level, transforms) Import Drag-and-drop importer with background loading and progress Python In-process Jupyter kernel plus a full editor (syntax highlighting, completions, terminal) Workspace Named variables, inspector, load/save .med workspaces Extensions Discover installed extension packages or drop-in folders; load, show, and unload without restarting the a
Toolboxes PyEditor, ImportData, and FilePreview open as central tabs and share the workspace.
Extensions Add UI and tools with pip packages — no core patch required.

Requirements Windows, macOS, or Linux CLI installer: a network connection — Python is downloaded for you pip install: Python 3.11 or later Scientific stack (NumPy, SciPy, scikit-image, pydicom, h5py, PySide6, and others) — installed automatically with the package

Install Pick your options below and the command updates to match. The CLI installer downloads a portable Python runtime with uv (no system Python needed) and creates launchers and shortcuts; pip and uv install with a package manager you already have. Only the core medics package is installed — add extensions separately afterwards. Install method CLI installer pip uv Your OS Windows macOS Linux Terminal Command Prompt PowerShell Python version 3.11 3.12 3.13 Desktop icon Create Skip Launch after install Yes No Run this command Copy curl -L -o "%TEMP%\medics-install.bat" https://medical-image-co
Verify After installing (either method), confirm the package and CLI are available: bash Copy python -c "import medics; print(medics.__version__)" medics --help

Launch bash Copy medics # or python -m medics Useful CLI commands: text Copy medics Start the application medics --create-ext [NAME] [DIR] Scaffold a new extension medics --build-ext [OPTIONS] Build an extension wheel medics --version, -V Print the installed version medics --help Show CLI help

Toolboxes Toolbox Role PyEditor Python IDE: syntax highlighting, completions, AST outline, integrated terminal, run against the Jupyter kernel ImportData Unified importer for DICOM, TIFF/PNG/JPEG, HDF5, MAT, NumPy, CSV, and related formats; background workers with progress FilePreview Read-only preview of text, code, markdown, spreadsheets, 2-D images, and volumetric data (DICOM series, stacked TIFF) JupyterLab Full JupyterLab web UI in a central tab. Its kernel runs MedICS's own Python environment, exposes the live workspace as ws , and needs no setup — notebooks, completions, and the debugge

Install an extension bash Copy pip install medics-ext-volume-viewer medics Loaded extensions appear under the Extensions menu and, if they provide a UI, can open a tab or window. Enable, disable, and inspect them from the extension manager dialog. Installed with uv instead? Use uv pip install … . The Extensions manager. Browse the extensions installed in MedICS, enable or disable each one, reload it after an update, and see what it adds to the interface.
Official extensions Maintained by the MedICS Team and published on PyPI . Install one with pip , then open it from the Extensions menu (windowed extensions open as a central tab).

Volume Labeler Medical Imaging Annotate 3D volumes: paint labels on B-frames / enface, constrain work to a slab with boundary curves, inspect in 3D, and export label maps. pip Copy pip install medics-ext-volume-labeler
Volume Viewer Visualization 3-D and 2-D volume visualization with GPU-accelerated rendering and multi-planar reconstruction (MPR). pip Copy pip install medics-ext-volume-viewer
Image Labeler Medical Imaging Annotate 2-D images with multiple label types and annotation workflows. pip Copy pip install medics-ext-image-labeler
OCT Viewer Medical Imaging OCT / OCTA visualization and analysis. pip Copy pip install medics-ext-oct-viewer
Retinal Layer Segmentation Medical Imaging Automated retinal layer segmentation with quantitative features. pip Copy pip install medics-ext-retinal-layer-segmentation

GraphicPy Visual Programming Node-based visual programming for building and running computational graphs. pip Copy pip install medics-ext-graphicpy More official extensions are in development. Browse all published packages on PyPI , or see the wiki for the full catalogue. Update one later with pip install --upgrade medics-ext-volume-viewer .

Create your own extension bash Copy medics --create-ext # or with a name: medics --create-ext medics-ext-my-tool A typical layout of an extension: text Copy medics-ext-my-tool/ ├── medics_ext_my_tool/ │ ├── __init__.py # ExtensionInterface implementation │ ├── extension.json # Display metadata │ └── ui/ │ └── main_widget.py # Optional PySide6 widget ├── tests/ ├── pyproject.toml └── README.md

ExtensionInterface Every extension implements: python Copy def get_name(self) -> str: ... def get_version(self) -> str: ... def get_description(self) -> str: ... def get_author(self) -> str: ... def get_category(self) -> str: ... def initialize(self, app_context) -> bool: ... def cleanup(self) -> None: ... def show_extension(self) -> None: ... initialize(app_context) receives the running MedICS application instance, so the extension can use the workspace, config, event bus, menus, and docks.
extension.json json Copy { "name": "My Tool", "version": "1.0.0", "description": "Does XYZ", "author": "Your Name", "category": "Image Analysis", "enabled": true, "windowed": true, "icon": null }

Entry point ( pyproject.toml ) toml Copy [project.entry-points."medics.extensions"] my_tool = "medics_ext_my_tool:MyToolExtension" Lifecycle in short: discover → initialize(app_context) → menu/toolbar action → show_extension() → cleanup() on unload.

Build and publish Run from the extension project directory: bash Copy medics --build-ext # plain Python wheel (default) medics --build-ext --protect # Cython-compiled, source-stripped medics --build-ext -p # same as --protect medics --build-ext --upload # build, then upload to PyPI (you must have an PyPI account) medics --build-ext --upload --test-pypi

Full notes: docs/extension-system.md and

What MedICS is MedICS (Medical Image Computing Suite) is a desktop application for loading, inspecting and analyzing medical images. Image viewing, Python scripting, data import and third-party tools all live in one window instead of being spread across separate programs.

Key features Area What you get Image I/O Open DICOM (including JPEG 2000 and OCT series), TIFF stacks, NIfTI, HDF5, MATLAB .mat , PNG/JPEG, video and more. Preview Inspect images, volumes, tables, Markdown and code — with slice navigation and window/level, without changing the file. Import Load image sequences, single files and whole DICOM folders, with drag-and-drop and background progress. Python An interactive console and the PyEditor IDE share one live workspace. Workspace Keep every result in a named workspace and save it to a .med file. Toolboxes FilePreview, ImportData, PyEditor and Jup

Supported formats Type Formats Images PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF, WebP, ICO, PPM/PGM/PBM, SVG, single-frame TIFF Volumes NIfTI, MetaImage, DICOM series, stacked TIFF, MedICS image bundles Scientific containers HDF5, MedICS .med , MATLAB .mat , NumPy .npy / .npz Tables CSV, TSV, Excel, Parquet Documents Markdown, plain text and source code Video MP4, AVI, MKV, MOV, WebM, WMV, M4V, MPG/MPEG, OGV, 3GP
The panels Show or hide panels from the View menu. Interface & components → File Explorer Variables Logging Jupyter console Terminal Agent chat

The toolboxes Built-in tools that open as tabs. Toolboxes → ImportData — load images and volumes. FilePreview — preview images and volumes. PyEditor — the Python editor. JupyterLab — notebooks in a tab.
Read the guide Looking for more? Extensions shows how to add tools to MedICS, and the MedICS Wiki has community tips and examples.

The MedICS window MedICS opens as a single window. Your tools open as tabs in the middle, and the panels around them give you the file tree, your variables, the log, a terminal and the Python console. Panels can be shown or hidden, resized and re-arranged. Show or hide panels from the View menu, or double-click a tab title to collapse the surrounding panels and focus on your work. The MedICS window. Tools open as tabs, with the File Explorer, workspace variables and the bottom panel (Logging · Terminal · Jupyter · Results) around them. The window is built from six regions: Region What it holds

Menu bar Menu What is in it File Open Folder… ( Ctrl + O ), Open Workspace… , New Window ( Ctrl + Shift + N ), Save , Save As… , Exit ( Ctrl + Q ). View Focus Mode ( F11 ), Theme (Dark / Light), the panel toggles — Show Explorer , Show Terminal , Show Logging , Show Variables , Results — and Agents Window ( Ctrl + Shift + A ). Toolboxes A checkbox for each toolbox; ticking it shows or hides that toolbox's Activity Bar icon. Extensions A checkbox for each installed extension, then Open Extension Manager… . Image Image-processing operations — type conversion, thresholding, transforms, Z-projecti

Activity Bar The vertical strip on the far left. From top to bottom: the Explorer (tooltip File Explorer ), one icon for each loaded toolbox (tooltip Open <name> ), one icon for each loaded extension , and the Settings gear at the bottom. Click an icon to open its tab; click it again to bring the tab back to the front. Drag toolbox and extension icons to reorder them. The core icons (Explorer, Settings) stay in place. Right-click the strip for a menu that shows or hides each toolbox and extension icon.

File Explorer Browse the folder you are working in. Double-click a file to preview it in a tab, drag files or folders into the window to import them, and right-click for the full set of file actions. On startup. It opens on the folder you were last working in; the toolbar switches folders. The current folder. Double-click a file to preview it, or right-click for Open , Copy path and Reveal in Explorer . At the top, Open Editors lists the files you currently have open — click one to bring its tab to the front. Below it is the folder tree. When no folder is open the panel shows No Folder Opened

Workspace Variables Every value you create in Python — arrays, images, tables and other objects — is kept in the workspace and listed here. Double-click a variable to inspect or preview it. Variables. Everything in the workspace, with its name, value and type. Double-click an entry to inspect or preview it. Each row shows the variable's name / index , its value and its type . The list is live: a variable created in the console, in PyEditor or in a notebook appears here straight away. Action How Inspect or preview Double-click a row — images and volumes open in a preview. Use a variable elsewhe

The bottom panel The bottom of the window is one dock shared by four tabs — Logging , Terminal , Jupyter and Results . Click a tab to switch, and drag the splitter to resize. Each tab is shown or hidden from the View menu.

Logging The in-app output panel shows messages from every part of MedICS. Logging. Messages from every part of MedICS, filtered by level, with buttons to clear the view or export the entries to a text file. Control What it does Level selector Filters the view by severity: ALL , DEBUG , INFO , WARNING , ERROR , CRITICAL . CLEAR Empties the visible log and the buffer behind it. EXPORT… Writes the log to a text file (default name exported_log.txt ). Entries read time [LEVEL] message and are colour-coded by level.

Terminal A real shell embedded in the window. It runs in its own process, separate from the application, so it is the place for command-line tools and scripts. Terminal. A shell in its own process, with a list of open shells on the right to switch, rename, clear or close them. Control What it does Terminal list One row per open shell, named after the shell. The active row is highlighted. Clear (⊘) Clears that terminal's scrollback. Kill (✕) Ends that shell. + New Terminal Opens another shell; a picker offers Command Prompt , PowerShell , Windows PowerShell or Git Bash on Windows, and the login

Jupyter console An interactive Python console that runs inside MedICS, so it shares your workspace — NumPy, Matplotlib and the scientific stack are ready to use, and ws is a handle to your variables. Jupyter console. An interactive Python console that shares your workspace, so anything you create here appears in Variables straight away. Type in the input area — the prompt reads In [N]: — and use: Key Action Enter Run the current cell. Ctrl + Enter Edit in multiple lines. Shift + Enter Force-run a multi-line cell. Tab Complete the name you are typing (variables, functions, attributes, dictionar

Results When a measurement or results extension is installed, the Results tab lists its table. The toolbar has Export… (writes the table to a CSV file) and a status line showing the row and column count. Click a column header to sort; right-click for Copy , Recalculate selected and Check calibration .

Status bar The strip along the bottom of the window reports what is happening — short messages such as Loading… , Settings applied successfully or an error. On the right sits the calibration badge : it reads no image when nothing is calibrated, otherwise a short summary of the current image's pixel spacing, slice thickness, frame time and units. Click it to set the scale.

Agent chat The AI assistant docks on the right as the Chat panel, and also opens in its own window. Ask questions about your data, or hand off a task and it will use the tools it needs — actions that change data ask for your approval first. Agent chat. The assistant docked beside your work — ask a question, or hand off a task and watch each step. See AI assistant for the full guide.

Settings & preferences Open preferences from the Settings gear at the bottom of the Activity Bar. On macOS it is also in the application menu as Preferences… , and the Extensions menu has Open Extension Manager… , which opens this dialog on its Extensions tab. The chat settings open the same dialog on its Chat / Agent tab. Preferences. Appearance, window behaviour, logging, chat and the MedICS token, grouped in a single dialog. The dialog is split into four tabs: Tab What you set there General Theme, logging and window behaviour. Extensions Install, update, enable and remove extensions. Chat /
General
Appearance Two mutually exclusive choices — Dark Theme and Light Theme . Choosing one applies it immediately so you can preview it, and the choice is saved with the rest of your preferences.

Logging Control What it does Log level How much detail is written: DEBUG , INFO , WARNING , ERROR or CRITICAL . Default: INFO . Log file The full path to the log file. Use Browse… to pick one; the platform default is shown as a hint. Changing the log level takes effect straight away.

Window Control What it does Use native menu bar (macOS/Linux) Draws the menus in the operating system's own menu bar where the platform supports it. On window close What happens when you close the main window: Ask me when I close the window , Quit MedICS completely , or Keep running in the system tray . The first time you close the window, MedICS asks you to choose; the answer is saved here. Quitting from the tray menu always exits completely.

Chat / Agent Everything the AI assistant needs: which model provider to use, your key, and how the assistant is hosted. Your API keys are stored separately from the other settings and are never committed anywhere.

Agent UI Control What it does Show agent window button and Chat panel Shows or hides the whole assistant chrome — the Agents Window menu item and shortcut, the menu-bar button, and the right-hand Chat panel. Applied immediately. Agent Harness Which assistant runtime to host: MedICS Harness (the built-in chat), DeepSeek Harness (a local WebUI), or OpenCode (a local WebUI). WebUI URL Read-only. Shows the address of the embedded harness, or that the MedICS harness has no embed URL. Restart / Reset status Recycle the harness host, or just clear the current run's status without remounting the chat

Provider & model Active provider selects which service the assistant uses. Pick one, then fill in its card: Provider You provide ChatGPT (OpenAI) API key, model. Gemini (Google) API key, model. Claude (Anthropic) API key, model. Grok (xAI) API key, model. GitHub Copilot Sign in with GitHub (no key to paste), model. Ollama (Local) Base URL and model; Discover lists the models your local server offers. DeepSeek API key, model. Custom (OpenAI-compatible) Base URL, optional key, model. In each card: API key — enter the key; use the eye button to show or hide it. If a key is already saved, its last
Conversation Settings Control What it does Temperature How creative the replies are, from 0.00 to 2.00 . Lower is more focused. Max tokens The longest reply the assistant may produce.

System Prompt The instructions prepended to every assistant prompt. Edit them to change the assistant's behaviour, or use Reset to default to restore the built-in text. Keys are saved to your MedICS home folder in .secrets.ini , separate from the other settings. The Open .secrets.ini button opens that file in your text editor.

Extensions Extensions are installed and managed from this tab — the same place the Extensions → Open Extension Manager… menu item opens. The Extensions tab. Every installed extension with its status, plus the packages available to install. The list has two parts: Section What it shows Installed Each extension with its version, its package name and a status: Shown (loaded and visible in the menu and toolbar), Hidden (loaded but not shown), or Not loaded . Available on PyPI Packages you can add, with a short description and an Install button. For each installed extension: Button What it does Loa
MedICS Token Where you check and enter your MedICS license token.

License Information Read-only fields describing the current license — Token ID , Email , Plan Type , Start Date , Expire Date , Last Checked and Status . The status reads Free mode — no token configured before a token is entered, and ✓ Valid once one is validated.

Validate Token Paste a token — the format is XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX — and click Validate to check it with the license server; a valid token is saved automatically and the License Information above is refreshed. The section also links to how to request a token.
Remove Token Remove Token returns MedICS to Free mode: free-tier extensions stay available, while paid features are disabled until a valid token is entered again.

Toolboxes Toolboxes are the built-in tools that ship with MedICS. Each opens as a tab in the central area — from the Toolboxes menu, from the activity bar, or by double-clicking a supported file in File Explorer. Toolbox What it is for FilePreview Read-only preview of images, volumes, tables, Markdown and code. ImportData Load raw stacks, image sequences, DICOM, NIfTI, MAT/NumPy and video into the workspace. PyEditor A Python editor and terminal that run against the live workspace. JupyterLab The full JupyterLab UI in a tab, running MedICS's own Python environment.

FilePreview Preview any file without changing it: 2-D images, DICOM and NIfTI volumes, TIFF stacks, tables (CSV, TSV, Excel, Parquet), Markdown, and source code. For image and volume views you can move through slices, adjust window/level , zoom and pan, and apply flips, rotations and transposes. FilePreview. A volume open in a tab, with the toolbar on top and the slice / window-level controls above the image.

Opening a file Double-click a file in the File Explorer — non-text files open here. Right-click a file and choose Open (or Open in FilePreview for a text file). Drag & drop one or more files onto the window from the operating system or the Explorer. Click Open… ( Ctrl + O ) on the toolbar and pick one or more files. Drop a variable from the Variables panel to preview data that is only in memory. Each file opens in its own inner tab. Re-opening a file just activates its tab; the Welcome tab comes back when every file tab is closed.

Toolbar Button Shortcut What it does Open… Ctrl + O Choose one or more files to preview; each opens in its own tab. Zoom In — Magnify the view. Zoom Out — Shrink the view. Reset View — Fit the image or volume back into the window and clear any pan and zoom. Flip Vertical — Checkable. Mirrors the image top-to-bottom. Flip Horizontal — Checkable. Mirrors the image left-to-right. Transpose — Checkable. Reflects the image across the main diagonal (swaps the axes). Rotate 90° clockwise — Cycles 0° → 90° → 180° → 270°; the current angle is shown on the button. Plane: — For volumes, which plane is di

What you can preview Kind Formats Images .png , .jpg , .jpeg , .bmp , .gif , .webp , .ico , .ppm , .pgm , .pbm , .svg , and single-frame .tif / .tiff Raw OCT volumes .oct , .octa , .foct , .ssada Data containers .mat , .med , .h5 , .hdf5 , .npy , .npz Volumes .dcm / .dicom , .nii / .nii.gz , multi-page .tif / .tiff Video .mp4 , .avi , .mkv , .mov , .webm , .wmv , .m4v , .mpg , .mpeg , .ogv , .3gp Tables .csv , .tsv , .tab , .xlsx , .parquet Markdown .md , .markdown , .mdown , .mkd Text / code .txt , .log , .json , .xml , .yaml , .yml , .py , .c , .cpp , .java , .js , .ts , .m , .r , .sh , .jl

The image & volume viewer Control What it does ◀ / ▶ and the slice slider Page through the volume; the counter reads current / total . Play / Pause Run the frames as a cine loop (disabled when there is only one slice). fps spin box Playback speed, in frames per second. W: and L: Window and level — the brightness and contrast of the display. These are display-only and are not saved into the data. Histogram A grayscale bar on the right; drag its handles for the same effect as the W/L spin boxes. Auto Levels Reset the window and level to the automatic range. Properties Open the File Properties di

Tables & Markdown Tables show a row-count label ( N rows × M columns ), sort when you click a column header, and filter as you type in the Filter rows… box. Markdown opens rendered, with Rendered / Source buttons to switch between the formatted view and the raw text.

Mouse & keyboard Action Effect Mouse wheel over the image Previous / next slice. Ctrl + wheel Zoom. Left-drag Pan. Right-drag Zoom. Right-click the view The view's own menu (fit, reset). Hover Live pixel readout in the status bar. PageUp / PageDown Jump ten slices back / forward. Home / End First / last slice. ← → ↑ ↓ One slice back / forward. + / - Zoom in / out. 0 Fit to window. The status bar shows the preview kind and file name on the left, and the pointer readout (for example (col, row) = value ) on the right.

ImportData Load images and volumes into the workspace. Choose how the source is structured, let the importer read and preview it, then send the result to the workspace. Imported data appears in the Variables panel. ImportData. Choose the Data Type , set the parameters, preview the frames, then Send to ws .

Data type Mode Use it for Volume Data A single volume read from a raw/binary stack file or a container ( .mat , .npy , .npz , NIfTI, DICOM, video). Image Sequence A folder or a set of image files stacked into one volume, in file-name order. The parameters below the selector change with the mode.

Volume Data parameters Field What it sets Image type The pixel type of the raw file — 8-bit , 16-bit Signed , 16-bit Unsigned , 32-bit Signed/Unsigned , 16/32/64-bit Real , 24-bit RGB/BGR , 32-bit ARGB/ABGR or 1-bit Bitmap . Width / Height The size of one frame, in pixels. Frame The number of frames in the stack. Offset to first Image Bytes to skip at the start of the file before the first frame (for a header). Gap Between Images Bytes to skip between consecutive frames. permutation How the three axes are ordered in the file (for example 0,1,2 ). Read Order F (Fortran), C or A — how the file's

Image Sequence parameters Control What it does Folder Shows the folder being read. Type a path or use the buttons below. Open Files Pick individual image files to stack. Open Folder Load every file in a folder (natural-sorted, so 2 comes before 10 ). Filter / Regex Choose how the pattern is matched, then type it in the box (for example *.* or *.tif ). Select All Tick every file in the list. Range — from : to Select a contiguous range of frames by index. File list The matched images, with check-boxes; only ticked files are stacked.

Preview & transfer Control What it does Frame slider + spin box Scrub through the frames of the loaded volume; the label reads current / total . Image area Shows the frame under the pointer; move the pointer to read the pixel value ( X:… Y:… ▶ value ). Send to ws Send the loaded volume to the MedICS workspace. Generate Function Write a Python loader for the current file — a ready-made function you can reuse. It opens a Generated Load Function dialog you can save.

What you can import Image sequences — folders or sets of TIFF, PNG, JPEG and similar frames. Volume files — DICOM ( .dcm / .dicom ), NIfTI ( .nii / .nii.gz ). Containers — MATLAB .mat , NumPy .npy / .npz and MedICS .med files. Video — .mp4 , .avi and similar load as a stack of frames. Raw/binary stacks — any file read with the Volume Data parameters above.
Drag & drop Drop files or a folder anywhere on the window. Several image files (or a folder) are treated as an image sequence; a single volume file is opened as Volume Data .

Status bar The green status bar along the bottom reports progress and messages ( "File loaded successfully!" , "N files found in the folder" ), the pointer pixel readout, and — for a raw stack — a byte-match badge that confirms the header/offset settings add up ( "✔ All bytes matched" ).

PyEditor A Python editor in a tab, with syntax highlighting, code completion, an integrated terminal and a set of code-navigation tools. Run (F5) executes your script against the live console, so it can use the variables already in your workspace. PyEditor. The editor with its toolbar, a breadcrumb bar, and the Ln / Col readout in the status bar.

Toolbar & tabs Button Shortcut What it does New Ctrl + N Open a new, untitled editor tab. Open — Open a file in a new tab ( .py is offered, but any file can be opened). Save Ctrl + S Save the active tab; an untitled tab asks for a path first. Run in Jupyter F5 Run the selection — or the whole file when nothing is selected — in the Jupyter console. Each file is a tab; a modified tab shows a * . Save As… ( Ctrl + Shift + S ) writes to a new path. Right-click a tab for Close Tab , Close Other Tabs , Close All Tabs and New Tab ; a breadcrumb bar above the editor shows the file's folder path, and C

Editing features Feature What it gives you Syntax highlighting Python and many other languages (C/C++, Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, JSON, YAML, XML, HTML, CSS, SQL, R, Shell and more). Code completion Python-aware suggestions as you type, with parameter hints for functions. Hover documentation Hover a name to see its documentation. AI ghost text Inline code suggestions; press Alt + \ to ask for one and Tab to accept it. Find & replace Ctrl + F to find, Ctrl + H to replace. Brackets & folding Auto-closing brackets and quotes, matching-bracket highlighting, and collapsible code blocks. Minimap &

Code navigation Action Shortcut What it does Go to Definition F12 / Ctrl +click Jump to where the symbol is defined. Peek Definition Alt + F12 Show the definition inline, without leaving the file. Find All References Shift + F12 List every use of the symbol in the References panel. Rename Symbol F2 Rename the symbol under the cursor. Go to Symbol Ctrl + Shift + O Jump to a class, function or variable by name. Go to Line Ctrl + G Jump to a line number. The References panel opens when you run Find All References . It lists the symbol, line and file; double-click a row to open that file at that l

Running code Press F5 (or click Run in Jupyter ) to run the selected text, or the whole file when nothing is selected. The code runs in the Jupyter console at the bottom of the window, so it sees the same workspace variables you do; the output appears in that console. A per-selection run is also bound to F9 .

Integrated terminal Ctrl + ` shows or hides the terminal — a real shell inside a tab. The + New Terminal button starts another one; a shell picker offers Command Prompt , PowerShell , Windows PowerShell and Git Bash . Each terminal row in the list has buttons to Clear or Kill it, and right-clicking the list gives Rename , Kill Terminal and Clear . The terminal is a shell for convenience — use the Jupyter console when you want your workspace variables.

Reviewing agent edits When the AI assistant changes a file you have open, PyEditor shows the changes inline with a small toolbar — ↑ / ↓ move between changes, and Accept , Reject , Accept All and Reject All keep or undo them.

Keyboard shortcuts Shortcut Action Ctrl + N New tab Ctrl + S / Ctrl + Shift + S Save / Save As F5 / Shift + F5 / F9 Run in Jupyter (file or selection) Ctrl + ` Toggle the terminal Ctrl + F / Ctrl + H Find / Replace Ctrl + / Toggle line comment F12 · Alt + F12 · Shift + F12 · F2 Definition · Peek definition · References · Rename Ctrl + Shift + O · Ctrl + G Go to symbol · Go to line Alt + \ · Tab Trigger / accept an AI inline suggestion

JupyterLab The full JupyterLab interface, embedded in a tab. It runs on MedICS's own Python environment, your workspace is available inside notebooks as ws , and it needs no setup — notebooks, completions and the debugger work out of the box. Install it into MedICS's environment to enable the tab (see Get started ). JupyterLab. The JupyterLab interface in a MedICS tab; the Launcher shows the available notebook environments.

The two environments When you start a new notebook or console from the Launcher , two environments are on offer: Environment What it runs MedICS (this environment) The default. The same Python interpreter as MedICS itself, so every package MedICS uses is already importable. It is wired into the live application: your workspace is available as ws , and the familiar scientific names (NumPy, Matplotlib and friends) are ready to use — the same starting point as the Jupyter console. Figures render inline. Variables you create here appear in the Variables panel. Python 3 (ipykernel) A plain Python k

AI assistant MedICS includes an AI assistant that can answer questions and carry out tasks. You can ask it about the data you have open, or ask it to do something and it will use the tools it needs — reading files, running Python, driving the toolboxes — and report back. Actions that create or change data ask for your approval first. The assistant appears in two places, and both share the same conversations: Surface What it is Chat panel Docked on the right of the main window. Toggle it from View → Show Chat . Agents Window A separate window ( Ctrl + Shift + A , or View → Agents Window ). Use

Using the chat Type your request in the composer at the bottom and send it with Enter . While the assistant works, each step it takes appears in the conversation. The composer: Control What it does @ Add context Attaches files or folders as context. Attachments appear as chips — click a chip to remove it. Mode How the assistant behaves this turn — see the table below. Model Which model answers. The menu also has Refresh model lists and Configure providers and API keys… . Send / Stop Sends the prompt; while the assistant is running, the same button stops it. Prompt box Where you type. Its borde

Approvals & permissions When the assistant wants to run something that could change your data, it stops and shows an ACTION REQUIRED card with the tool, the reason and its arguments, and buttons to decide: Button What it allows Allow once Runs this one action only. Allow for run Allows this tool for the rest of the current run. Always allow Remembers the choice for this tool in future runs. Allow all this session Allows every tool until you restart MedICS. Deny Refuses the action. If you do not answer within a few minutes the request is denied automatically. A mode-switch request instead offer

The Agents Window The assistant in a window of its own, with the conversation beside a session list and a workspace panel. The Agents Window. The assistant in a window of its own, with the conversation list on the left and the transcript beside it. Its header, left to right: Button What it does History Shows or hides the session list ( Ctrl + B ). Workspace folder Shows the folder the chat is attached to; click to change it. Tools Opens Tools & permissions . Calendar Opens Scheduled tasks . Graph Opens the Token usage dashboard. Add Starts a new session ( Ctrl + N ). Refresh Reloads the chat s

Sessions & history Every chat belongs to a repository — a folder you opened in MedICS — so the list in the Agents Window is grouped by folder. Use the Search box to filter by title or content, and the right-click menu on any chat to Open , Rename… , Duplicate or Delete it. Several chats can be deleted at once. A folder's menu lets you start a chat there, pin it to the top, or remove it from the list. Two extras use the same assistant: Scheduled tasks (the calendar in the Agents Window) run a prompt in the background on a schedule — you give each task a name and a prompt, and choose how often i

What it is good at Answering questions about your images, tables and variables. Running Python against your live workspace. Driving the toolboxes for you — opening a tool, importing, previewing. Multi-step tasks that combine the above.

Configuration Choose the provider and model and enter your API key in Settings → Chat / Agent . The assistant is optional — MedICS works fully without it. Chat settings. Pick the provider and model, enter your API key, and set the temperature and maximum tokens the assistant may use. The Chat / Agent tab holds the Active provider and its key and model, the Temperature and Max tokens , and the System Prompt — the instructions sent with every request. The same tab also chooses the Agent Harness and shows or hides the assistant chrome. See Settings & preferences for each control. The assistant's

Overview Retinal Layer Segmentation runs on OCT volume for segmenting retina. It runs a deep-learning model on every B-scan, detects the retinal layer boundaries, reconstructs them into smooth curves, and builds a 3-D view of the layers across the volume. Everything runs locally. Your data never leave the machine. The extension opens its own window, titled RetinalLayerSegmentation . Retinal Layer Segmentation. A data source and control panel on the left, and four linked views on the right.

What you can do Load OCT and OCTA volumes, load any previously saved segmentation. Segment the retina with one click, on the GPU if available. Review the detected boundaries, show or hide individual layers, and correct any boundary by hand. Interpolate the segmentation across sparse B-scans to fill the whole volume. Inspect the result as B-scans, en-face projections and a 3-D surface. Send the curves and masks back to the MedICS workspace, or save them to files.
Requirements MedICS, installed and running. GPU is required for accelate AI retinal layer segmentation.
Install Install the extension from inside MedICS, the Settings-> Extension .
Open the Extension Manager In MedICS, open Extensions → Manager… from the menu bar.
Find the extension Scroll the list to Retinal Layer Segmentation .
Install it Select the extension and click Install , then wait for the download to finish.
Enable it If it is not already enabled, click Load . The extension then appears under the Extensions menu, and show on the Activity Bar .
First run Open Retinal Layer Segmentation . Click the icon shown on the Activity Bar .
Quick start
Open the extension From the Extensions menu or Activity Bar , open Retinal Layer Segmentation . The RetinalLayerSegmentation opens.

Load data Option 1: On the File tab pick your OCT volume (and optionally OCTA), then click Load Data — or drag files onto the window. Option 2: Drag the file from System File Explorer to extension window. Option 3: Drag the loaded variable in Workspace (ws) to extension window
Segment Click Run AI Segmentation . Adjust ROI to make sure retinal tissue is included inside the ROI . Choose the compute device if you want to run on a different device.
Review & correction Hide or show layers, and use the corrector to fix any boundary.
Save Use Save to WS to send results to the MedICS workspace, or Save to write files.

The Retinal Layer Segmentation window The window has two areas. The left panel holds everything you operate; the right side shows four linked views of the data. Loaded volume. An OCT volume loaded and segmented; the four views show the corresponding frames.

Data source The top of the left panel loads input data. It has two tabs. Data source. The File and Save to WS tabs at the top of the left panel. Switching tabs between File (load) and Save to WS (transfer).

File tab Choose a file for each input with its folder button, or type the path, then click Load Data to read them together. Field What it loads Formats OCT The OCT volume (B-scans) .foct , .oct , .dcm , .mat , .tif / .tiff OCTA An optional OCTA (angiography) volume, co-registered with the OCT .ssada , .octa , .dcm , .mat , .tif / .tiff Segment A previous segmentation (layer curves) .json , .dcm , .mat , .med Array orientation matters. When a .mat file is loaded, its volume must be stored as nframe × nrow × ncol — B-frames along the first axis, rows (depth) second, and A-scans (columns) last. T

Load Data Settings The setting… button on the File tab opens Load Data Settings . This is where you choose which loader function reads each kind of file. Open it when a file is not recognised, or to teach the extension a custom format. Load Data Settings. Pick a loader function on the left, assign it to OCT, OCTA or Seg, and set the file patterns it should handle. How to use it: Select a loader function in the list on the left — its source appears in the preview below. Click OCT >> , OCTA >> or Seg >> to assign the selected function to that input. Type the file patterns the loader should handl

Save to WS tab Transfer what is currently loaded back into the MedICS workspace under the names shown. Edit a name if you want a different one, then click the >> button in that row. Row Transfers Default name OCT The loaded OCT volume oct_data OCTA The loaded OCTA volume octa_data Segment The segmentation (curves/retinal layer boundries) seg_data

Drag and drop Drop supported OCT, OCTA or segmentation files anywhere on the window. Files are matched by their name and routed to the right input automatically; you can also drag a variable out of the MedICS Workspace Variables panel and drop it on the window to load it. This extension also support drop a image sequence (same image type) as OCT / OCTA volume data.

Frame & resolution Control What it does Frame The B-scan currently shown. Use mouse wheel or use the arrows to move through the volume; every view follows. total Read-only total number of frames in the loaded volume. Upate data resolution Opens a helper to set or correct the physical resolution (pixel size, scan width/height/depth) so measurements and the 3-D view are to scale. Useful when combining volumes acquired at different scales.

Scan Resolution Upate data resolution opens the Scan Resolution dialog. It converts the physical size of the scan into a per-pixel resolution so that measurements and the 3-D view are to scale. Scan Resolution. Enter the physical scan size and the axial resolution; the lateral resolution is calculated as you type. Enter the two required values and the lateral resolution updates live. Click OK to write the new resolution to the loaded data. Element What it does Scan size in mm (width, height) The physical width and height of the scan in millimetres. Required. Axel resolution The axial (depth) r

Region of interest Restrict processing to a vertical band of each B-scan — this speeds segmentation up and avoids the empty space above and below the retina. Control What it does ROI top / bottom The first and last row (in pixels) that the segmentation will use. Auto Estimates the retinal band automatically from the loaded OCT and fills in the values.

Segmentation controls These controls drive the AI model and the manual refinement. They sit below the data and preprocessing groups. Segmentation controls. Run AI Segmentation, sparse mode, device, corrector, interpolation and save.

Run AI Segmentation Runs the deep-learning model on every B-scan and fills in the layer boundaries. If a GPU device is available you are asked which one to use; otherwise it runs on the CPU. Progress and any errors are reported in the status bar .

Device Chooses how the model runs. AUTO picks the best available device; named entries are the GPUs found on the machine; CPU always works. If a GPU fails, the extension falls back to the CPU automatically.

Corrector Selects the manual editing tool. All correcting happens in the Right B-Frame (the OCT panel). Choose a tool from the Corrector dropdown — None for review only, or one of the three editing tools below. First decide how the target boundary is chosen: Selection mode How the boundary you edit is chosen correction: auto The boundary nearest the pointer is edited. correction: select The layer chosen in the en-face dropdown is always edited, wherever the pointer is. The selection mode is set from the Right B-Frame context menu (see B-Frame context menus ). The correctors are available in th

Liner Draws a straight segment over the boundary — the quickest way to correct a short span. Hover over the boundary to focus it; it thickens while the other boundaries dim. Click the left mouse button at the start of the segment, then drag to the end point. A straight line follows the pointer and replaces the curve between the two points. During correction, click left mouse button to reset the start point of the segment. Double click left mouse botton to stop and apply correction. Only the dragged span changes; the rest of the boundary stays as it was.

LiveWire Traces the strongest image edge between two points — best when the boundary is clearly visible in the image but awkward to draw by hand. Hover over the boundary to focus it. Click the left mouse button at the start point, then move the pointer along the boundary. The tool keeps computing the lowest-cost path along the image edges and redraws the curve as you move. During correction, click left mouse button to reset the start point. Double click left mouse botton to stop and apply correction. Because it follows image edges, LiveWire can be pulled off-course by speckle or fluid; re-trac

Anchors Edits the boundary point by point, by dragging its control points (the small square markers). Use it for precise, local adjustments. Hover over the boundary to focus it — its control points appear. Move mouse to a control point to select it; the cursor marker snaps to it. Hold the left button and drag to move the point. The curve refits through the anchors as you drag. While dragging, scroll the mouse wheel up to add the neighbouring points on each side to the selection (they move together), and scroll down to drop them again. Right-click the panel while Anchors is active for these ent

Interpolation Control What it does Interpolation Step How far apart the segmented key frames are (minimum 2). Used when filling a sparse volume. Interpolation Turns interpolation on or off. Restart Interplation Clears the interpolation and recomputes it from the current boundaries. mask when recomputing, instead of discarding it.
Save Saves the current segmentation to a file (curves and, optionally, the fluid mask). To send the result to the MedICS workspace instead, use the Save to WS tab.

Layer boundaries The Layer boundaries group lists every boundary the model can detect. Tick a box to show and export that boundary; use the small dropdown next to it to choose how it is drawn (dashed or solid line). Select All toggles every boundary at once. Layer boundaries. Each boundary has a visibility checkbox and a line-style dropdown; Select All is at the bottom. Only the boundaries that default to On are produced by the AI model. The entries that default to Off — PVD, GCL/IPL, ELM, IZ/RPE and SAT/HAL — are listed for completeness but are not implemented in the auto-segmentation model .

The views The right side is split into four linked views. Moving the frame — or picking a point — keeps them in sync. Left B-Frame and Right B-Frame. The same B-scan shown with the layer curves overlaid; Right B-Frame is the editable one. En-face and 3-D. An en-face projection of the layers, and an interactive 3-D surface of the segmented volume. View Shows Left B-Frame A single B-scan with all visible layer curves drawn over it. Right B-Frame The editable B-scan — the corrector tools work here. En-face A top-down projection. The Layer / OCT / OCTA button cycles the projection, and the neighbo

View toolbar Each view has a small toolbar. Hover a button to see what it does. Button Action Hide Curves / Show Curves Toggle the layer curves over the B-Frame image. Fast / Slow Scan View Switch the interpretation of the second Left B-Framexis between fast-scan and slow-scan, which changes how the two B-frames and the en-face view relate. Transpose ON / OFF Swap the horizontal and vertical axes of the image views. Layout Stack the B-frames or place them side by side. Reset Reset the camera / zoom of the view. Collapse Hide the left or right side so a view can fill the window.

B-Frame context menus Right-click inside a B-Frame panel to open its context menu. The two panels differ: the Left B-Frame (OCT / OCTA overlay) focuses on display and export, while the Right B-Frame (the editable OCT panel) also offers the corrector tools. Left B-Frame (OCT / OCTA overlay). Display, export and workspace actions. Right B-Frame (OCT). Adds the corrector tools and correction modes. Left B-Frame (OCT / OCTA overlay) Item Action View All Fits the image back into the panel — resets any pan and zoom. Line weight ▸ Curve thickness submenu — pick 1 px to 8 px . Save image... Saves the

Status bar The bar along the bottom reports where the pointer is and what the data is. Status bar. Pointer position, pixel value under the pointer, the volume shape, and its dtype. Readout Meaning Pointer position Where the pointer is in the hovered image, in data coordinates. index The pixel value under the pointer. Shape The loaded volume's shape (frames × rows × columns); shows No data loaded before you load anything. Dtype The volume's data type. One-off messages — loading, saving, warnings — also appear here.

Keyboard shortcuts The window has no menu bar; these are the keys you can use while working. Keys Action ↑ / ↓ Previous / next B-scan. ← / → Jump ten frames back / forward in the main window; in the layer view, jump by the current Interpolation Step. Ctrl (hold) With the pointer over a view in Slow Scan view, moving the pointer scrubs through the volume (see below).

Mouse & interaction Action Result Move over a B-frame or en-face view Updates the pointer readouts in the status bar. Ctrl + move in a B-frame (Slow Scan view) Scrub through the volume: the horizontal position selects the corresponding slice/frame in the other views. Click in the 3-D view Picks the surface point under the pointer and moves the B-frames and en-face indicator there. Drag in an image view Pans the image (use the mouse wheel to zoom). Click a boundary in Right B-Frame Selects that boundary for editing with the chosen corrector . Drag / rotate in the 3-D view Orbit, zoom and pan th

Menus & context menus Menu Where Contains Extensions menu In the MedICS main window Opens the Retinal Layer Segmentation window. B-Frame context menu Right-click inside a B-Frame panel Display, export, corrector and workspace actions — see B-Frame context menus . En-face context menu Right-click over the en-face view The plot's own menu; MedICS hides its default entries, so it exposes no actions — use the view toolbar instead. Loader context menu Right-click an entry in Load Data Settings Delete — marks the loader function as deleted so it is no longer offered. The window itself has no menu ba

Saving & exporting Goal How Use the result in other MedICS tools Save to WS tab → send oct_data , octa_data and seg_data . Write the segmentation to disk Save in the control panel. Keep the fluid mask Tick Keep Fluid volume before saving/recomputing.

GPU acceleration & troubleshooting Segmentation is far faster on a supported GPU. It uses an ONNX Runtime model with an optional NVIDIA CUDA provider. GPU acceleration needs the driver, the ONNX Runtime build and the CUDA/cuDNN libraries to match each other. Symptom What to do Log says CUDA is unavailable; runs on CPU A CPU-only ONNX Runtime is installed. Install onnxruntime-gpu (and remove plain onnxruntime ) on Linux/Windows with an NVIDIA GPU. Crashes on a Conv node ( CUDNN_* errors) The CUDA stack is loaded but the cuDNN kernels do not support this GPU, or the cuDNN version does not match

Notes & limitations Only boundaries produced by the model are drawn; a few listed boundaries are placeholders. Automatic CPU fallback means a too-old GPU still yields a result, just more slowly. Sparse volumes must be interpolated to obtain a dense segmentation. The segmentation is computed locally; no image data is uploaded.

Overview Volume Labeler annotates 3-D medical volumes. Paint labels directly on the cross-sections or on the top-down projection, keep the work inside a layer slab so you never mark the wrong tissue, measure how much of each label you have drawn, and save the result as a label map for later use. Everything runs locally — your data never leave the machine. Volume Labeler. The load and label panel on the left, the painting toolbox along the top, and the B-frame, en-face and 3-D views filling the rest of the window.

What you can do Load a volume, an optional second volume, boundary curves, and a previously saved label map. Paint labels freely with a brush, or let a threshold tool pick the voxels for you. Limit painting to a retinal slab defined by an upper and a lower boundary curve. Paint on the en-face projection to label whole columns through the volume at once. Keep several named label maps and a palette of label classes, each with its own colour. Read the volume and area of every label as you work, and keep free-text notes. Inspect the labels as a 3-D rendering, then save the maps to a file or the wo
Requirements MedICS, installed and running. Python 3.11 or newer.
Install Install the extension from inside MedICS — no command line needed.
Open the Extension Manager In MedICS, open Extensions → Open Extension Manager… from the menu bar.
Find the extension Scroll the list to Volume Labeler .
Install it Select the extension and click Install , then wait for the download to finish.
Enable it If it is not already enabled, click Load . The extension then appears under the Extensions menu and on the Activity Bar .
First run Click the Volume Labeler icon on the Activity Bar to open it.
Quick start
Load a volume Click Load Data… and choose a volume, or drag a file onto the window. If a volume is already open you are asked whether to Replace it or Overlay the new one.
Add boundaries (optional) Click Load Boundaries… to load layer curves, then pick the Upper and Lower layers. This limits painting to a slab.

entries.section: Choose a map and a label
entries.text: Choose a map and a label In the left panel select a label map and a label class (its colour).
Paint Pick Brush (or another tool) in the toolbox and paint on B-frame A , B-frame B , or the en-face view.
Review Step through frames and check the Value tab and the 3-D viewer as you go.
Save Click Save… to write the maps to a file, or Save to WS to send them to the MedICS workspace.

The Volume Labeler window The window is a set of panels around the volume. The left panel loads data and manages maps and labels; the toolbox across the top holds the painting tools; the rest shows the volume. Area What it is for Left panel Load the volume, boundaries and label maps; manage the label maps and label classes. Toolbox The painting tools, their size and shape, the cleanup steps, and the measurement / note tabs. B-frame A The left cross-section — the volume as an underlay, with an optional second volume and the labels on top. B-frame B The centre cross-section — the primary volume
Loading data The left panel. Loading controls at the top, the label maps below, and the label classes at the bottom.

Loading a volume Click Load Data… to choose a file, or drag files and folders onto the window. If a volume is already open, MedICS asks what to do with the new one. Choice Effect Replace Clears the current labels and loads the new volume in their place. Overlay Keeps the current volume and layers the new data on top of it as a second (overlay) volume. Cancel Does nothing. Supported volume formats include .med , .tif / .tiff , .mat , .oct , .foct , .dcm and .img . A file whose type is not obvious opens the Select Data Type dialog, where you say whether it is Volume Data , an Overlay , Label Dat

Companions loaded automatically When a volume loads, the extension looks next to it for related files and loads them too: File What it is <name>_lmp.tiff or <name>_lmp.med A saved label map (the newest is preferred when both exist). Boundary files — seg.mat , _seg.mat , segmentation.mat and their .med forms Layer curves for the upper and lower boundaries. <name>.ssada and other second-volume siblings A second volume drawn as an overlay on B-frame A.

Boundaries Click Load Boundaries… to load layer curves ( .json , .mat , .med , .dcm ). Then choose the Upper and Lower layers and, if needed, nudge each one with its offset. The slab between them drives the en-face projection and shades the B-frames, so painting stays inside the tissue you care about. See Frames & the slab .

Label maps Click Load Label Map… to bring back a saved map ( .tiff , .med , .mat , .png ). Maps written by this extension store their data under a label tag, so they reload without any extra questions. You can also drop a label file onto the window, or load a labelled array from the workspace.

Load Data Settings The Settings… button opens Load Data Settings . Use it when a file is not recognised, or to teach the extension a custom format. It works the same way as in the Retinal Layer Segmentation extension. Load Data Settings. Pick a loader function, assign it to Data, Label Map or Boundary, and set the file patterns it should handle. Element What it does Loader list Every loader function found in the custom-loader folder, shown as module.function . Select one to assign it or preview its code. Remove / Delete Marks the selected function as deleted so it is no longer offered. Add fro
Label maps & label classes

Label maps A label map is one full 3-D labelling of the volume. You start with a single map called Default , and you can keep several — for example one per structure, or one per annotator. Column / button What it does Name The map's name. The selected map is the one you paint into and the one the 3-D viewer shows. Edit (pencil) Opens Edit Label Map to change the name and description. Delete (trash) Removes the map after a confirmation. At least one map must always remain. Add… Opens Add Label Map to create a new, empty map — or a copy of an existing one. Load Label Map… Loads maps from a file.

Label classes The Label list holds your paint classes. The extension starts with 32 ready-made labels, each with its own colour; the first six are the classic primaries (cyan, yellow, green, red, blue, magenta). The active label — marked with a dot — is the value every tool writes. Column / button What it does Label The class name. Click a row to make it the active paint label. Color The class colour swatch; click it to change the colour. Edit (pencil) Opens Modify Label to change the name, colour and description. Add Label… Adds a new class. Add Label. Name the class, choose its colour, and d

The toolbox The toolbox runs along the top of the window. It holds the tool size and shape, the cleanup steps that tidy a stroke, the painting tools themselves, and two tabs — Value and Note . The toolbox. Size and shape, the cleanup steps, the painting tools, and the Value / Note tabs.

Size & shape Control What it does Tool size The brush diameter, in pixels (1–500; default 25). Shape The brush outline — disk , square , rod or ellipse . Angle The orientation of the rod and ellipse shapes, in degrees (0–359). You can change the size and angle without leaving the image: scroll the wheel to resize, and hold Alt while scrolling to rotate.

Cleanup Control What it does Fill holes Fills holes smaller than this many pixels inside a stroke. Set it to 0 to leave holes alone. Region filter Removes connected regions smaller than this many pixels, cleaning up stray specks (default 25). Propagation How many frames the ← / → keys jump (default 5).

Painting tools Exactly one tool is active at a time. Click a tool to turn it on; click it again (or press its key) to turn it off. Tool Key What it does Brush Q Paints the active label under the pointer as you drag. ChangeLabel W Repaints pixels that already carry a label to the active label — handy for fixing a wrong class. T-Min E Labels pixels darker than the value you click, plus the “v +” offset. T-Max R Labels pixels brighter than the value you click, plus the “v +” offset. T-Range T Labels pixels within a value window around the value you click (a low and a high offset). The three thres

Painting Choose a tool in the toolbox, make sure the right label and map are selected, then paint on B-frame A , B-frame B or the en-face view. Painting with the brush. Drag the left mouse button to draw the active label; the stroke is committed when you release. Mouse action Result Left-drag Applies the active tool — paints the current label (or runs the threshold / change-label tool). Right-drag Erases the label under the pointer. Middle-click Undoes the last stroke. Wheel Changes the tool size. Alt + wheel Rotates the tool angle. Ctrl + wheel Zooms the view. Ctrl + drag Moves the frame indi

Painting on the en-face view The en-face view is a top-down projection through the current slab. Painting there marks a whole column of the volume at once — the fastest way to label a vertical structure across many frames. The yellow line marks the frame currently shown in the B-frames; drag it to change frames. The en-face view. A projection through the slab; paint here to label whole columns, and drag the indicator to change the frame.

Frames & the slab The Boundaries bar sets the slab and the current frame. The boundaries bar. Choose the Upper and Lower layers, offset each one, and step through frames. Control What it does Upper The layer that bounds the slab from above, plus an offset in pixels. Lower The layer that bounds the slab from below, plus an offset in pixels. Frame The B-scan currently shown (1-based) and the total number of frames. Keys Action ↑ / ↓ Previous / next frame. ← / → Jump back / forward by the current Propagation step. Stepping through frames. Moving the frame updates the B-frames and the en-face indi

The views Two cross-sections, one en-face projection and one 3-D rendering. They stay in sync as you move through the volume. B-frame B (OCT). The primary cross-section with the labels on top — the main place to paint. B-frame A (OCTA). The same cross-section, with an optional second volume drawn as a colour overlay. View Shows B-frame B The primary volume and the label overlay. B-frame A The volume with an optional second volume drawn on top, and the label overlay. En-face A top-down projection through the slab, with the labels and the current-frame indicator. 3-D An interactive 3-D rendering

Per-view controls Each image view has a small toolbar above it. Control What it does Low / High The contrast window: the low and high values mapped to black and white. Colorbar The greyscale (or overlay) ramp; click it to choose a different colour map. Show/Hide label Turns the label overlay on or off. Transparency How strongly the labels show through the image (0 = invisible, 1 = fully opaque). Projection On the en-face view: Mean , Maximum , Minimun or Thickness . The mode replots the projection. Label transparency. Lower the value to see the image underneath the labels. En-face projection m

B-frame context menu Right-click inside a B-frame for display and export actions. The B-frame context menu. Boundary visibility, image and label exports, and Save to ws . Item Action Show/Hide upper boundary Toggle the upper curve over the image. Show/Hide lower boundary Toggle the lower curve over the image. Save image… Save the current frame as an image. Save stack image… Save the whole stack as an image. Save label… Save the current frame's label overlay. Save stack label… Save the whole stack's label overlay. Save image with label… Save the current frame with the labels drawn on it. Save s

The 3-D viewer The 3-D dock renders the active label map (not the raw volume), so you can orbit a shape and confirm a label is where you expect it. Its toolbar has a mode selector, a lighting preset and a camera reset. Control What it does 3D / Enface Switches the dock between the 3-D rendering and the overlay-volume en-face (enabled once a second volume is loaded). Lighting One of Headlight , Three Lights , Ambient or Studio . Reset Camera Returns the camera to its default view. Drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, and use the on-screen axis gizmo to re-orient the camera. If 3-D rendering is unavai

Measurements & notes The toolbox has two tabs next to the tools. Tab What it shows Value A table of measurements for the active map. Each label gets a column, with rows for Volume (voxels) and Area (pixels) , and each cell also shows the percentage of the total. Note A free-text box. What you type here is saved together with the label maps. The measurements update as you edit labels, in the background, so the window stays responsive while you paint.

Saving & exporting Save… opens Save Label Map As with a default name of <volume>_lmp . Pick a format: Format What it stores TIFF ( .tiff / .tif ) All maps stacked along the frame axis, with the colour map and a description in the metadata. MAT ( .mat ) The maps, label definitions, notes and descriptions under a label tag. MED ( .med ) The same label payload in MedICS's own format. MedImage ( .medimage / .medimg / .mi ) A full image bundle of the session. Save to WS instead asks for a workspace variable name (defaulting to the current map's name) and stores the maps there, ready for other MedIC

Status bar The green bar along the bottom reports what is happening. Readout Meaning Background tasks Short notes such as Syncing enface to volume or Updating measurements while work runs in the background. Mouse position Where the pointer is over the image. Pixel value The value under the pointer. Data summary The volume number, its shape, data type and value range, plus the second volume's shape when one is loaded. One-off messages — loading, saving, warnings — also appear here.

Keyboard shortcuts Keys Action ↑ / ↓ Previous / next frame. ← / → Jump by the current Propagation step. Q Toggle the Brush tool. W Toggle the ChangeLabel tool. E Toggle the T-Min tool. R Toggle the T-Max tool. T Toggle the T-Range tool. Space (hold) Temporarily hide the label overlays. Ctrl (hold) Navigation mode — the pointer scrubs frames instead of painting.

Mouse & interaction Action Result Left-drag in a view Applies the active tool (paints, or erases with the right button). Right-drag Erases labels under the pointer. Middle-click Undoes the last stroke. Wheel Changes the tool size. Alt + wheel Rotates the tool angle. Ctrl + wheel Zooms the view. Ctrl + drag Scrubs frames via the indicator. Drag in the 3-D view Orbits the rendering; scroll to zoom. Right-click a B-frame or en-face Opens that view's context menu.

Notes & limitations A label map is a full 3-D volume, so large volumes use a lot of memory; the 3-D view is refreshed in the background to keep painting smooth. Painting on the en-face view updates the 3-D label volume in the background; the sync follows shortly after you release the mouse. Non-square volumes are shown square in the en-face view; painting maps back to the true size automatically. The 3-D viewer renders labels, not intensities — it is a way to check labels, not to review the image. Everything is computed locally; no image data is uploaded.
